messages:
Ravi: Brainstorm: introduce a 'lateral buffer' that diverts excess tenant traffic into a cheap/degraded execution lane instead of hard 429s. Aim: smooth bursts and protect core P99. Quick takes?
Nia: Sounds promising. Is this just a queue or does it change execution (smaller model/longer latency)?
Ravi: Both. Buffering + degraded model. Buffer TTL very short (3-7s). Degraded model = smaller embedding/cheaper quant profile.
Omar: Important: token/accounting semantics. We must bill these differently and make it obvious in traces. Suggest metric `buffered_units` and trace tag `lateral_buffer=true`.
Priya: Abuse concern: adversaries could route probing into the buffer to skirt quota checks. Need per-tenant buffer_budget and an abuse_score gate. If abuse_score > threshold disallow buffer.
Jules: Interface: ingress returns `Buffer-Token` header when diverting. Runtime picks it up and chooses degraded path. If downstream doesn't support the token, fail fast so we don't silently do wrong work.
Nia: Failure semantics for clients: if buffer path returns a special code (e.g., 524) meaning 'served degraded, non-retryable'. Expose a `retryable:false` flag to avoid retry storms.
Omar: Ops: we should alert on sustained buffer depth > X and on buffer_eject_rate. Also track `buffered_latency_ms` histogram.
Ravi: Rollout plan: start with internal tenants, flag behind feature flag, exempt reserved/dedicated customers. Alpha rollout with simulated noisy tenants to validate fairness.
Priya: Add a small budget drain while in buffer so it's not free. Could deduct at lower rate so customers still see cost but less than full price. Billing needs a SKU proposal.
Jules: I'll draft a lightweight proto: `{ admit: bool, token: string, mode: "degraded"|"buffer", retryable: bool }` as a string in the RFC. Keep TTL short and token single-use.
Nia: Simulation: I'll run mixed-tenant traffic with and without buffer and measure p99 delta and cost. Need hooks to emulate degraded-model latency.
Omar: I'll add trace spans for buffer admission and runtime handling. Also make sure services unaware of buffer tokens explicitly reject.
Ravi: Good. Next: Priya writes billing/console changes, Nia owns sim, Jules drafts RFC with proto and safety gates, Omar handles traces. We'll reconvene after RFC draft.
